question: Do public default-branch code searches reveal canonical ERC-8056 integration markers in a purposive sample of wallets, portfolio/explorer interfaces, and EVM libraries?

primary_sources.fact: ERC-8056 is a Draft standards-track ERC. Standard ERC-20 functions remain raw; uiMultiplier() supplies the scaled UI amount semantics.
Robinhood Stock Tokens keep raw balances static while the onchain multiplier changes the shares-per-token ratio for dividends and splits.
Robinhood's REST /prices surface is raw underlying-equity price, while currentMultiplier is exposed separately.
The Chainlink Stock Token feed already reports underlying equity price multiplied by uiMultiplier().

github_search.method: Connected GitHub code search, scoped to the listed public repositories. Searches reflect GitHub's indexed default-branch code at observation time.

positive_control.purpose: Confirms that the same repository-scoped search path returned indexed code for an ordinary token-balance identifier.

github_search.result: No matches for the eight canonical ERC-8056 markers in this nine-repository search.
github_search.interpretation_boundary: This is an integration signal, not proof that any named product lacks runtime support. Support can exist in private services, generated code, third-party metadata, dynamically constructed calls, unindexed branches, or code that uses different identifiers. The sample is purposive and not population-representative.

suwappu_prechange_search.current_control: Canonical Robinhood Stock Token trading is fail-closed in Suwappu pending a dedicated jurisdiction/eligibility flow, so this search finding is not evidence of a currently exposed Suwappu trading path.

official_split_fixture.kind: documentation example, not an observed market incident
